# Jack Xing

> Jack (Huihao) Xing works in data science and analytics: define the metric, test what the data can support, and turn it into a decision. M.S. Data Science, Boston University. Currently at WY Industries.

This site presents four case studies, each traced from the first question to what changed. Figures are rates or ratios; business volumes, spend and client names are withheld.

## Case studies

- [Search ads got 44% cheaper. Should the brand spend more?](https://huihaoxing.github.io/paid-search.html): Search-ads pilot measured against on-site conversion. 2.7% of ad visitors took a next step versus 17% of other visitors (7.3% on the same page). Management paused the broad-match ads on that analysis, and the site was rebuilt for generative engine optimization; it now ranks first for its core category search on Google, Gemini and ChatGPT.
- [Boston’s buses look on time. Why do some riders wait so long?](https://huihaoxing.github.io/rider-wait.html): Rider-side wait-time measure across 20M+ MBTA boardings on 15 routes, built with a BU Spark! team for GBH News; the project team adopted it as its primary reliability measure. Route 14 riders averaged 16+ minutes.
- [AI lead research, with a person in control](https://huihaoxing.github.io/sales-ai.html): LLM prospecting pipeline on Claude and OpenAI, exposed as an MCP server. A human approves every model spend; outputs are JSON-schema verdicts with public citations; the system has no send path. Review time per lead fell from about 15 minutes to 2 to 5.
- [Weather, events and Green Line delays in one table](https://huihaoxing.github.io/transit-pipeline.html): Master's team project. Green Line arrivals, weather and events joined on one hourly clock with Azure Data Factory and Spark (bronze, silver, gold), one reusable delay table; a model on it reached a 3.56-minute mean absolute error.
